b1.central_visual_idea: The release tears off. The maintenance stays attached. Three illustrated repository work sheets each have a detached 'FEATURE WORK / SHIPPED' section above them. The substantial remainder still carries migrations, dependency upgrades and coverage gaps. Shipping has removed the celebratory part, not the underlying workload.
b1.how_it_communicates_the_problem: The matching torn edges make the separation visible without arrows or explanation. Repeating the remaining workload across three repository sheets makes this an estate-wide problem, rather than one forgotten ticket. These are deliberately constructed paper work artifacts, not black bands of engineering words, a task-board screenshot or an exact accounting of a customer's backlog.
b1.why_devin_role_is_clear: The sheets depict the buyer's unresolved work, not work Devin claims to have completed. A separate, prominent capability line names the response: 'Devin playbooks for recurring maintenance.' The approved support supplies the cross-repository scope. The Devin signature and Contact sales CTA identify the product and next action without turning the illustration into product evidence.

production.how_the_layer_is_used: Construct the work-sheet illustration as exact SVG paths with Satori, Resvg and Sharp. Its visual meaning depends on matching tear profiles, readable workload labels and repetition across repositories; generation would add variability without improving that meaning. Use flat white paper, ink outlines and two offset backing leaves beneath each remaining sheet. No shadows, photographic texture, perspective, folded-corner document icons or decorative dimensional objects. Composite all type separately. Render at 2x and downsample for delivery. Coordinates below describe top-left layout boxes; use the supplied Inter files, explicit line breaks and no automatic fit-to-box shrinking.

b1.legibility_at_360px: The headline reads at approximately 25px in portrait and 23px in square. Maintenance nouns remain approximately 11px in both, with feature and repository labels at 10px. The tear separation remains approximately 11–15 display pixels; the detached sections must visibly belong to the sheets below. The illustration occupies the middle of the ad rather than floating in a large empty field. At feed size, the viewer must recognize shipped sections above repeated unresolved repository workloads before reading the explanatory support. Test both final rasters at 360px, not only enlarged exports.
reject_if: A five-second unprompted read does not identify both 'feature work shipped' and 'maintenance still remains across repositories.'
The detached feature pieces read as unrelated cards because the matching tear profiles or vertical separation disappear.
The artifact reads as three ordinary UI cards, a task board, outlined document icons or arbitrary strips of engineering nouns.
The remaining sheets are mostly blank, or the headline and footer leave the illustration too small to carry the concept.
Paper texture, shadows, perspective or ornamental styling turns the work artifacts into decorative stationery.
Any workload noun clips, wraps differently between columns or is reduced below the specified size to fit.
The illustration implies Devin shipped these features or has already resolved the maintenance.
Any invented repository name, task ID, customer evidence, result, code, screenshot, completion check or metric appears.
The Devin playbooks capability line or approved cross-repository support is missing.
Pricing, customer logos, capacity claims or endorsement language appears.
Critical text leaves the safe area, or a Brand-Lock violation remains after one corrected render.

a1.central_visual_idea: One dependency-update assignment becomes a returned review packet. The same named chore appears on the assignment and on the proposed change, so the viewer sees delegation and return—not merely reprioritization.
a1.revised_direction: Deterministic illustrated work artifacts, not generated imagery. Keep the exact headline 'Hand off the dependency update.\nYou review the PR.' in the upper third. Fill the middle with two substantially overlapping paper artifacts: a smaller assignment slip at upper left reading 'DEPENDENCY UPDATE' and 'Assigned to Devin'; a larger returned packet in front at lower right reading 'DEPENDENCY UPDATE', 'Proposed change by Devin' and 'For your review'. The repeated task title and physical overlap provide continuity without an arrow. The returned packet has two broad, clearly labeled sections, 'Diff to inspect' and 'Tests to review'; these are artifact labels only, with no invented code, test output or pass status. Place 'Workflow illustration' visibly beside the artifact. Keep the locked support 'You write the ticket. Devin opens the PR with the diff and tests.' beneath it, followed by the black 'Get started' CTA to https://app.devin.ai/. Use 36px minimum for the three role-bearing labels. The packet—not blank space—is the visual center.
reject_if: The viewer can identify the chore but cannot tell it was assigned to Devin and returned for developer review.
The assignment reads as a backlog priority card, or the return looks like a second unrelated task.
The illustration includes fabricated code, a PR number, branch names, timestamps, test results or authentic-looking product controls.
Tests are depicted as automatically passing or the proposed change is marked accepted, completed or merged.
Arrows or outline document icons do the explanatory work.
The exact headline, support or Get started CTA is replaced; pricing is added.

a2.central_visual_idea: Devin authors the change; the developer marks up the review copy. A large open review packet makes the execution role and the decision role visible on the same artifact.
a2.revised_direction: Deterministic-only. Keep 'Devin opens the PR.\nYou decide if it merges.' above a large open paper spread, explicitly labeled 'Workflow illustration'. The left page is headed 'CHANGE PROPOSED BY DEVIN' and carries two substantial labeled areas, 'Proposed changes' and 'Test evidence'. Do not fill these with simulated code or invented evidence. The facing page is headed 'YOUR REVIEW' and carries the exact support as three large editorial review instructions: 'Read the diff.' / 'Run the tests.' / 'You keep the merge.' One sparse blue side-rule emphasizes the developer's review instructions; it is not a status indicator. The left page establishes Devin as author, while the facing page establishes human inspection and judgment. Make these roles at least 36px, with the support at 42px. Keep the spread free of app chrome, checkboxes and accept/reject buttons. Place the separate black 'Get started' CTA below, linking to https://app.devin.ai/.
reject_if: Devin appears to be the reviewer of human-written code rather than the author of the proposed change.
The execution and review roles require explanatory notes outside the ad to understand.
Blank areas overwhelm the artifact, leaving another headline with a decorative rectangle.
The packet masquerades as a real PR, screenshot, session transcript or test report.
The review page includes a Merge button, completed approval or a claim that Devin can never auto-merge.
The visual implies that inspecting test evidence guarantees correctness, or adds pricing.

b2.central_visual_idea: A named customer's repository estate, with its custom operating mechanism attached to the number. Scale is the attraction; FE fundinfo's implementation is the qualification, not a footnote.
b2.revised_direction:
Deterministic-only. Retain the exact headline 'Devin playbooks.
1,800 repositories.' Make 1,800 dominant, but place 'FE fundinfo's implementation' immediately above the headline at 42px so attribution is visible in the first read. Under the number, construct a representative estate of 24 small, flat repository folios in a regular field, borrowing the work-artifact construction from B1 without torn feature sections. Do not label individual units or encode statuses. Add the visible caption 'Illustrative estate — not a repository count.' Below the field, set the implementation context at 36px/44px: 'FE fundinfo built custom automation
to run Devin playbooks across its estate

Fit by reducing the representative field, not the attribution or mechanism. No image-generation call: the useful visual information is estate repetition, not atmosphere.
reject_if: The number reads as Devin-wide scale, a typical result or an out-of-the-box deployment claim.
FE fundinfo attribution is separated from the figure or becomes a small legal footnote.
The custom automation and custom Replit apps context is omitted or replaced with a generic agent-fleet claim.
The representative units imply exact numerical encoding, completed jobs, simultaneous agents or universally merged changes.
The image contains the capacity result, any projection, pricing or another customer's evidence.
The customer logo appears, endorsement is implied, or the CTA leads somewhere other than the supplied customer story.

set_logic: The set now shares a language of substantial, plainly illustrative engineering work artifacts—not abstract black masses and not fabricated product interfaces. A1 is an assignment and returned packet; A2 is an authored change facing a developer's review instructions; B1 is shipped feature work physically detached from persistent repository workloads; B2 is a named implementation with a representative estate. Common rules: #F7F6F5 ground, #191919 ink, white artifacts, black CTAs, one sparse #317CFF intervention, Inter Regular/Medium/SemiBold and a plain-text Devin signature only. Headlines remain dominant, but the central artifacts must occupy enough of the frame to communicate without production notes. All approved headlines, support, CTAs and destinations remain locked; layout-only line breaks are permitted. No pricing anywhere in images or Meta copy: the marketer's later instruction supersedes the brand-kit commercial-copy requirement. Preserve approved Meta copy except for the explicitly rejected material. FE fundinfo's 10% result may appear only in attributed detail copy as its reported immediate increase in engineering capacity from automated test generation, security fixes and modernization work; do not invent a measurement timeframe. Remove the projection sentence entirely. A1/A2 depict human review as the advertised workflow, not a technical prohibition on auto-merge. Keep independent-project disclosure in the portfolio presentation and accompanying post. Render B1 first and approve it on visual comprehension, density and mobile legibility before extending the system. Brand-Lock failure requires rejection and one corrected render; a second failure fails the concept.
dropped_from_previous_direction: All image and Meta pricing, including quota qualifications and the commercial ladder: rejected as unverified and out of scope.
All projected customer figures and the projection sentence: removed from the packet, not moved into fine print.
The displaced dependency strip: it communicated prioritization but not assignment to Devin and return for review.
The abstract PR block, YOUR CALL lockup and explanatory gap: they required interpretation instead of showing authorship and review.
B1's empty feature slot and repeated black maintenance bands: absence and word repetition did not make shipped work versus remaining repository work sufficiently recognizable.
The exactly counted repository matrix and its count assertion: false precision in the illustration distracted from the actual named scope claim.
The replacement of B1's approved support with capability copy: the approved support is restored, with Devin playbooks identified separately.
Moving B2's approved support entirely off-image: it is restored, alongside prominent attribution and implementation context.
The requirement to obtain an unknown customer-story URL: the approved strategy already supplies the exact first-party destination.
The identical fixed header and footer coordinates across all frames: the set needs shared hierarchy, not a rigid template that produces empty typography cards.
Any use of the supplied references' Cognition lockup, generic arrow diagram or Book a demo CTA: these are not carried into the revised work.
